Camera and upper-body pose are controlled jointly via proxy-mesh renderings, giving independent control over expression, pose, and viewpoint. A camera-triplet training strategy makes the approach efficient: our models train for 34 hours on a single A100 using only public multi-view data. VDAs outperform state-of-the-art single-image 3D avatars on novel-view reenactment, reducing face LPIPS by 29% and improving perceptual quality (JOD) by 66% on BecomingLit. A static 3DGS reconstruction probe further confirms that our generations are the most multi-view consistent. Built on a video prior, VDAs produce effects beyond the reach of explicit renderers, including physically plausible hair dynamics, shadows, reflections, and refractions.

title: The Collection of a Real-World, Large-Scale Dataset for Automated Skill Evaluation in Central Line Dressing Change
summary: Central line-associated bloodstream infections (CLABSIs) remain a major source of preventable morbidity and mortality in healthcare settings. Proper execution of the central line dressing change (CLDC) procedure is essential for infection prevention, yet current approaches to competency assessment rely primarily on manual ob- servation by clinical educators, making evaluation time-intensive, difficult to scale, and limited in consistency and granularity. These challenges highlight the need for AI-assisted skill evaluation methods that can support more objective, reproducible, and scalable assessment of clinical performance. However, progress in this area has been constrained by the lack of broad-scale, clinically grounded datasets for developing and evaluating such methods. In this work, we present the collection process of a large-scale video dataset for CLDC skill evaluation, comprising 365 recordings of registered nurses collected during the 2026 annual competency exam at Houston Methodist Hospital. Each video is paired with subtask-level temporal annotations and clinical performance assessments spanning 17 subtasks of the procedure. We describe the data collection and curation pipeline, including pilot testing of record- ing configurations, annotation protocol design, and post-collection processing. We further establish the feasibility of video-based skill assessment through benchmark experiments with spatiotemporal deep learning models. This dataset provides a foundation for future research on automated clinical skill assessment, feedback generation, and AI-assisted training in nursing education.

title: Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models
summary: Video world models that generate and explore environments at scale need a persistent 3D memory of what they have produced. Plane primitives offer a natural candidate: a compact set of oriented planes captures the dominant structural elements (e.g., walls, floors, facades) of indoor and outdoor scenes, while requiring only 7 parameters per primitive. We present PPMem, a video world model that adopts plane primitives as its persistent 3D memory. PPMem augments a video diffusion transformer with a planar prediction head and a Depth Token Fusion (DTF) module: each autoregressive chunk jointly produces RGB video and planar geometry, which merges into a persistent plane memory that conditions subsequent chunks via rendered depth. The resulting memory is three orders of magnitude more compact than per-pixel point clouds (~100K primitives, 5MB for a full scene), geometrically explicit (metric depth, normals, exportable surfaces), cross-view consistent (jointly predicted by the shared backbone), and adaptive (refined by the merging procedure as generation proceeds). On DL3DV and RealEstate10K, PPMem outperforms prior 3D-grounded world models in video quality while jointly producing metric-scale depth, surface normals, and exportable planar geometry, sustaining coherence across hundreds of frames under large viewpoint changes. Project page: https://hyzcluster.github.io/ppmem.

title: StopWatch: Goal Grounding for Object-goal Navigation
summary: Pretrained VLMs bring rich world knowledge and semantic priors to object-goal navigation, and fine-tuning a VLM into a navigation policy has become a common recipe. Despite this progress, success rates remain low, and it is unclear which capability these fine-tuned policies lack. Our diagnosis identifies goal grounding as the dominant failure. These policies explore well, yet often fail to notice that the goal is already in view or to estimate how far away it is. To address this failure, we ground the goal explicitly. Explicit grounding substantially improves success and reaches state-of-the-art results on six benchmarks across three scene collections. We also correct annotation defects in these benchmarks, so that future methods are evaluated more faithfully. Our analysis on the clean benchmarks shows that, with ground-truth grounding, our policy nearly matches the expert that generated its demonstrations, leaving the headroom in perception rather than policy learning. Our work points to goal grounding as a missing piece of object-goal navigation and offers a simple and effective solution to the task.

title: Rethinking the design space of Vanilla Pixel Diffusion Transformers
comment: Project webpage: https://soumik-kanad.github.io/mflow-diffusion/. 33 pages, 23 figures, 15 tables. Submission under review
summary: Pixel-space diffusion models have recently re-emerged as a compelling alternative to latent diffusion, avoiding the lossy latent bottleneck and separately trained autoencoder. JiT shows that a vanilla diffusion transformer can generate directly in pixel space by replacing the commonly used velocity prediction ($\boldsymbol{u}$-prediction) with clean image prediction ($\boldsymbol{x_0}$-prediction). In this work, we revisit this choice and introduce MFlow, an adaptive parameterization that learns to interpolate between $\boldsymbol{x_0}$- and $\boldsymbol{u}$-prediction across principal directions of the data, learned end-to-end with diffusion training. We find that the preferred parameterization varies systematically with the data representation and model capacity -- notably, increasing model capacity shifts preference toward velocity prediction. We evaluate MFlow across ImageNet, UCF-101 video, and large-scale text-to-image generation, demonstrating competitive or improved generative performance across diverse settings. In addition, we find that vanilla pixel diffusion transformers, irrespective of parameterization, retain a persistent high-frequency deficit relative to real images. To address this, we introduce ConvRefiner, a lightweight convolutional module trained post-hoc with an adversarial loss while keeping the diffusion backbone frozen. With only a small amount of additional training, ConvRefiner restores the high-frequency statistics of generated images while preserving FID. Project webpage: https://soumik-kanad.github.io/mflow-diffusion/.

title: Learning to Correct Geometry in Generated Videos
comment: Accepted by NeurIPS 2026. Project page: https://weijielyu.github.io/VGC
summary: Generated videos often lose geometric consistency under camera motion: structures warp under viewpoint change, parallax becomes inconsistent, and smooth camera movement may collapse into shot-like transitions. We argue that this failure is largely a data problem. In web-scale video corpora, most visible motion comes from dynamic objects captured by static or weakly moving cameras, leaving only sparse supervision for viewpoint-induced appearance changes. To address this, we propose Video Geometry Corrector (VGC), a post-hoc video-to-video model trained on synthetic paired supervision. Starting from real videos with diverse camera motion and pose annotations, we construct VG-Pairs with a synthetic paired-supervision data generation pipeline. Each video clip is treated as a geometry-consistent target and paired with a distorted counterpart synthesized by a pretrained image-to-video inpainting model using trajectory-adaptive keyframes. VGC learns to map the distorted input to the geometry-consistent target without modifying the source generator, and uses optical flow as an auxiliary cue to help disentangle camera motion from object motion. Experiments on pose-conditioned and prompt-driven benchmarks show that VGC improves geometric consistency across multiple source generators, and scaling to a larger backbone further extends the framework toward more general video refinement.

title: ECHOES: Seeing Beyond the Current Image via Recursive History Compression and Privileged On-Policy Distillation
summary: Long-horizon GUI agents rely on visual history to maintain task states, but retaining historical screenshots increases visual-token usage and inference costs, while textual summaries can discard critical state information, undermining long-horizon reliability. We propose ECHOES, which leverages training-time privileged information to guide textual history compression and strengthen long-horizon reasoning. Specifically, ECHOES adopts a Compression-Think-Action (CTA) format to recursively update a textual history state and reason. The same model, given privileged multi-image inputs, serves as a teacher that provides dense token-level on-policy distillation on student-generated CTA rollouts. Our Perception-Memory Fidelity (PMF) Gap-guided OPD-RL framework dynamically balances privileged distillation and task-reward optimization, with periodic teacher updates supporting continued improvement. We further introduce ECHOESBMK, a fine-grained diagnostic benchmark derived from real GUI agent failure trajectories to jointly evaluate visual perception and cross-modal state retention. Experiments on four GUI benchmarks and ECHOESBMK demonstrate substantial gains in task performance and memory fidelity. Without retaining historical screenshots at deployment, ECHOES achieves competitive performance with a favorable performance-inference-cost trade-off and exhibits positive zero-shot transfer to unseen visual planning tasks.

title: DynamicVis: Dynamic visual perception for efficient remote sensing foundation models
summary: The continuous advancement of remote sensing technology has enabled high-resolution Earth observation; however, interpreting these expansive images using modern Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) remains a significant challenge. Unlike object-centric natural images, remote sensing imagery is fundamentally characterized by extreme target sparsity and massive spatial redundancy. Key objects of interest (e.g., ships, vehicles, scattered buildings) often occupy less than 1% of the spatial extent, surrounded by vast, target-free backgrounds. Many existing VFMs rely on uniform dense processing (e.g., Vision Transformers), while a substantial branch adopts pixel-reconstruction pre-training paradigms (e.g., Masked Autoencoders). These designs may waste substantial computational capacity on modeling redundant backgrounds and dilute the feature representations of small, sparse targets. To bridge this structural misalignment, we propose DynamicVis , a remote sensing visual foundation model explicitly tailored to spatial sparsity in high-resolution imagery, with a focus on large-scale visual pre-training and transferable spatial representations for diverse downstream perception tasks. Architecturally, DynamicVis introduces a Dynamic Region-Aware State Space Model (SSM) that bypasses uniform computation. It adaptively routes and incrementally models only task-relevant, high-salience tokens while employing a parameter-free integration for background context, drastically reducing the complexity of processing ultra-long 2D token sequences ( ∼ 100,000). Crucially, to equip the network with robust spatial-selection capabilities, we propose a novel weakly supervised Region-Level Meta-Embedding Multi-Instance Learning (MIL) pre-training paradigm. Trained on a million-scale dataset, this paradigm promotes foreground-aware regional discrimination in the latent semantic space, mitigating the semantic ambiguity of conventional pixel-reconstruction methods. Extensive evaluations across nine diverse downstream visual perception tasks reveal that DynamicVis achieves competitive performance across region-, instance-, and pixel-level remote sensing tasks, with particularly strong results in sparse-target and instance-level perception tasks (e.g., small object detection and instance segmentation). Notably, DynamicVis processes high-resolution imagery (2048 × 2048) with merely 97 ms latency and 833 MB of memory consumption without employing any acceleration techniques (approximately 6% and 3% of a base ViT, respectively), offering a favorable trade-off between computational scalability and representation accuracy for multi-granular remote sensing analysis. Source code is available at https://github.com/KyanChen/DynamicVis .

title: Global cross-modal geo-localization: A million-scale dataset and a physical consistency learning framework
summary: Cross-modal Geo-localization (CMGL) matches ground-level text descriptions with geo-tagged aerial imagery, which is crucial for pedestrian navigation and emergency response. However, existing studies are constrained by narrow geographic coverage and simplistic scene diversity, failing to reflect the immense spatial heterogeneity of global architectural styles and topographic features. To bridge this gap and facilitate universal positioning, we introduce CORE, the first million-scale dataset dedicated to global CMGL. CORE comprises 1,034,786 cross-view images sampled from 225 distinct geographic regions across six continents, offering an unprecedented variety of perspectives in varying environmental conditions and urban layouts. We leverage the zero-shot reasoning of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) to synthesize high-quality scene descriptions rich in discriminative cues. Furthermore, we propose a physical-law-aware network (PLANET) for cross-modal geo-localization. PLANET introduces a novel contrastive learning paradigm to guide textual representations in capturing statistical scene descriptors of satellite imagery. Extensive experiments across varied geographic regions demonstrate that PLANET significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, establishing a new benchmark for robust, global-scale geo-localization. The dataset and source code will be released at https://github.com/YtH0823/CORE .

title: Physics-driven semantic scattering structure understanding of aircraft target in SAR images
summary: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) has become indispensable for target interpretation owing to its all-day and all-weather observation capability. In SAR target interpretation, electromagnetic scattering information provides a physically grounded cue beyond visual texture and has been widely exploited for target interpretation. However, existing methods remain dominated by local scattering center representations. Such unordered and component-agnostic representations are highly unstable for aircraft targets. As a result, physically existing components with weak scattering responses are often missed, resulting in the incomplete reconstructed topology structure. To address this limitation, we establish Semantic Scattering Structure Understanding as a new paradigm for SAR aircraft interpretation. Semantic scattering keypoints are defined to associate local electromagnetic responses with physically meaningful aircraft components, while visibility-aware attributes are introduced to retain weakly observable yet physically existing components. The keypoints are further organized into a stable semantic scattering structure. Building upon this, we propose S 3 U-SAR, a physics-driven framework to localize semantic scattering keypoints and construct the complete representation constrained by multi-dimensional physical priors, including scattering heterogeneity, rigid-body topology, speckle uncertainty. A confidence-gated joint supervision strategy is further introduced to alleviate optimization conflicts. We construct KP-SAR-Aircraft-1.0, the first fine-grained benchmark for semantic scattering structure understanding. Extensive experiments demonstrate that S 3 U-SAR achieves the best performance compared with baselines. Class-disjoint cross-category and cross-dataset evaluations further verify its generalization capability and transferability. Notably, in downstream orientation estimation, the method improves P 1 ° and P 5 ° by 15.0% and 19.1% over the strongest baselines. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed representation paradigm in advancing SAR target understanding from implicit local response regression toward explicit global structural representation. The trained model and dataset will be available at https://github.com/YYF121/S3U-SAR .

title: GeoPhysAdapter: Scale-matched geophysical adaptation for cross-domain landslide mapping with vision foundation models
summary: Newly triggered landslides rarely carry immediate annotations, so cross-domain transferability determines the value of landslide mapping for emergency response and regional risk assessment. Vision foundation models have strengthened representational transfer, yet on unseen regions, events, and sources they still generate high-confidence false alarms. Terrain, material, and rainfall triggering can constrain such errors, but their supports are local, regional, and event-scale, so resampling onto a 10 m grid misaligns them with the segmentation decision unit and compounds the uncertain geographic context problem (UGCoP). We propose GeoPhysAdapter, which anchors on a frozen vision foundation model, restricts terrain, material, and triggering to dense spatial guidance, regional modulation, and event-timing forcing, and applies bounded adaptation at two decision units, the pixel and the candidate landslide body, reverting exactly to the visual prediction where support is insufficient. On an event-isolated PILD dataset of four public sources, 55 global landslide events, and 7890 test samples, 70.3% of cross-domain false-positive mass lies in near-pure spurious bodies of median equivalent diameter 207 m, matching coarse-prior support rather than the pixel. Pixel-level adaptation removes a net 507,817 erroneous pixels, reducing error by 7.76%, whereas raising the decision unit to the candidate body, under identical samples, anchor, and baseline, increases error reduction to 23.99% and improves IoU by a relative 14.2%. The gain decreases monotonically with terrain displacement, exceeds a strong optical control of spectral change and visual confidence alone by 0.019 IoU, remains positive across five vision anchors, and survives a pre-registered re-execution with a 20.61% error reduction. The binding constraint is therefore the match between the native scale of physical priors and the operative decision unit, not denser physical stacking. Data and code are publicly available at https://github.com/Liu-Zhihang/geophysadapter .

title: Cross-sensor continual maritime object recognition via spectral shift modulation in heterogeneous infrared–visible UAV imagery
summary: Multi-modal maritime object recognition is pivotal for UAV-assisted search and rescue. However, large-scale multi-platform UAV deployments inevitably encounter heterogeneous infrared sensors with diverse spectral response functions, leading to non-stationary multi-modal distributions and severe dynamic spectral shifts across successive multi-platform UAV deployment phases. Existing continual learning paradigms typically focus on mitigating catastrophic forgetting via memory replay, but overlook the sensor-specific biases inherent in spectral variations. Such biases induce negative transfer and performance degradation, as the model fails to decouple stable object features from dynamic spectral fluctuations. To address these challenges, we propose C3SM, a cross-sensor spectral shift modulation framework. The core of C3SM is a design-inspired spectral shift parsing prior that decouples sensor-specific spectral responses from sensor-invariant structural cues. By anchoring the fusion features to a structure-consistent reference space within the spatial-frequency domain, the proposed prior quantifies the cross-sensor discrepancy into a spectral shift index. Leveraging this proxy index, C3SM integrates a prior-guided cross-sensor memory modulation module. This module stabilizes the continual learning trajectory by adaptively suppressing unreliable high-shift memory experiences. Furthermore, a shift-robust contrastive learning strategy enforces feature alignment across spectral shift clusters, ensuring the capture of robust cross-sensor correlations. Extensive evaluations on the UAVSensorCL dataset across four heterogeneous sensors illustrate that C3SM achieves a 48.88% mAP at 7.15 FPS, outperforming state-of-the-art CODA-Prompt-PL (45.92% mAP) and ER-PL (45.09% mAP). By mitigating spectral interference, C3SM provides a robust baseline for maritime object recognition across dynamic environments. The dataset and code are available at https://github.com/Dingyuan-Chen/C3SM .

title: Constructive solid geometry for automatic topology-aware BIM reconstruction from point clouds
summary: The automatic reconstruction of Building Information Models (BIMs) remains challenging, especially when applied to multi-storey buildings and indoor environments with non-Manhattan layouts and curved structures. To address these challenges, this paper presents a novel method that places Constructive Solid Geometry (CSG) at the core of building reconstruction from point clouds. The methodology also integrates the Segment Anything Model (SAM) and knowledge-based rules to reconstruct as-built BIMs while preserving the geometry and topology of building elements. The proposed approach consists of two main stages: SAM-based segmentation and CSG-based modelling. First, SAM is used to segment rooms, as well as door and window openings. Solids are then generated for the indoor spaces and openings. Finally, a set of Boolean operations is applied to reconstruct building elements, including slabs, walls, indoor spaces, doors, and windows, while subtracting openings of doors, windows, and staircases. Finally, the reconstructed model is encoded with semantic information following the Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) schema. The method was evaluated on seven two-storey building point clouds and demonstrated strong performance, achieving a mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) greater than 90% for floor plan reconstruction, a precision above 87% for door and window detection, and mean geometric deviations below 8 cm for BIM reconstruction.

title: SkySplat++: Hierarchical 3D Gaussian Splatting for generalizable sparse-view reconstruction from multi-temporal satellite imagery
summary: Scene reconstruction from sparse-view satellite images remains a challenging task due to insufficient geometric constraints. While generalizable 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) methods have shown high efficiency for novel-view synthesis, existing methods are often unsuitable for satellite imagery due to incompatibility with the rational polynomial coefficient (RPC) model and limited generalization capability. In this work, we present SkySplat++, a hierarchical generalizable 3DGS framework that extends our previous SkySplat to further improve scene reconstruction. SkySplat++ refines Gaussians in a coarse-to-fine manner, enabling robust modeling of both large-scale scene structures and fine-grained texture details. To improve reconstruction under sparse-view conditions, a Height-Guided Hierarchical Cost Volume (HG-HCV) module is integrated to enable more accurate cost volume construction. Additionally, a hybrid height supervision strategy is employed to stabilize height estimation under radiometric inconsistencies. Compared to per-scene optimization methods, SkySplat++ achieves up to 36 times speed up over EOGS through feed-forward inference after training, while achieving higher accuracy. It also outperforms generalizable 3DGS baselines, reducing mean absolute error by 10.38–14.81 m relative to HiSplat across two benchmarks, and demonstrates strong cross-dataset generalization on the MVS3D test set. The code will be released at https://nancheng2001.github.io/SkySplatV2/ .

title: RT-ProtoNet: radiative-transfer-guided few-shot prototype networks for cross-region bathymetry in optically clear reef environments
summary: Satellite-derived bathymetry faces two coupled obstacles: labels are scarce, and models transfer poorly across regions. We propose RT-ProtoNet, a radiative-transfer-guided few-shot prototype network, which takes patches from three penetrating Sentinel-2 bands and treats ICESat-2 depths, aggregated to the 10 m grid, as sparse supervision; cross-region episodic meta-training then yields a transferable metric representation. Rather than embedding the radiative transfer relation as an analytic formula, we use it as a comparability criterion between support and query pixels, entering the attention as a learnable additive distance penalty. The prediction sums a convex combination over support depths and a base regression head trained on source domains only and frozen at deployment, so no target-domain parameters are estimated. We evaluate on five optically clear shallow reef regions by leave-one-region-out cross-validation against airborne laser bathymetry, against nine baselines, where K is the total number of support pixels (3, 5, 10, 20, 50). For K ≤ 20, RT-ProtoNet attains the lowest cross-region macro-mean RMSE (2.79–2.48 m), with a run-to-run standard deviation 0.67 times the runner-up’s; at K = 50, pre-training with head fine-tuning overtakes it. Ablation shows the residual head’s gain scales with support depth coverage (correlation 0.991) and that the two physical priors are largely substitutable; twelve perturbations to the attenuation input change RMSE by only 0.66%. The method suits depths of roughly 2–20 m and budgets of K ≤ 20, and does not extrapolate to turbid or optically complex waters. Independent evaluation at two external optical-domain sites, a moderately turbid embayment (Tampa Bay) and a clear-to-moderately-turbid transition site (Boquerón Bay), further delineates the method’s applicability across contrasting optical conditions, showing reliable transfer within the clear-water regime but substantial degradation under stronger optical attenuation.

title: UrbanQGS: Large-scale urban surface reconstruction via analytic curvature consistency in quadratic Gaussian splatting
summary: Large-scale 3D surface reconstruction at the city scale from UAV imagery is a core task for building digital-twin cities. Although 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) and its variants have achieved remarkable progress in radiance-field reconstruction, existing methods still struggle with scale-varying structural complexity and diverse urban textures: geometry is often incomplete in low-frequency, weak-texture regions over large areas, while in high-frequency regions with intricate details, disordered primitive distributions tend to cause floating artifacts and outliers. To address these issues, we propose UrbanQGS, a large-scale urban reconstruction framework built on quadratic Gaussian splatting. We inherit quadratic surface Gaussians as scene primitives and use their analytic curvature as the central driving signal to perform a two-stage geometric refinement: (1) A self-supervised geometric constraint based on cross-view curvature consistency, which effectively fills geometric holes in weak-texture planar regions. (2) A curvature-aware adaptive representation allocation strategy that reweights, recalibrates, and ranks densification gradients, guiding split and clone operations toward geometrically complex regions while standard pruning removes redundant primitives. In addition, we integrate a monocular normal prior to correct global orientation drift during large-scale reconstruction. We further assess the compatibility of UrbanQGS with partitioned large-scene reconstruction using a visibility-aware block-wise protocol with hardware-constrained per-block budgets. The blocks are trained sequentially on a single GPU. Experiments on large-scale UAV datasets demonstrate that, compared with state-of-the-art 3DGS-based large-scale reconstruction methods, UrbanQGS maintains superior geometric quality while substantially reducing redundant Gaussians and mesh complexity, yielding finer and more complete geometric structures, while qualitative results on our custom-collected dataset indicate its compatibility with a partitioned large-scene reconstruction pipeline.

title: N-PCLN: A physics-informed deep learning framework for short-term chlorophyll-a prediction with sparse satellite observation
summary: Chlorophyll-a (Chla) is a key indicator of lake eutrophication. Its short-term prediction is essential for water quality monitoring and bloom early warning. However, traditional deep learning models often rely heavily on dense observations and provide limited process interpretability. To address these limitations, this study proposes a physics-informed deep learning framework, named N-PCLN, for short-term Chla prediction in Erhai Lake. The framework integrates Sentinel-3 OLCI imagery and meteorological datasets from 2016 to 2024. It uses Chla, land surface temperature, wind speed, and precipitation as inputs. Total phosphorus is incorporated through a nutrient–phytoplankton model to construct a physical loss. This design enables the model to jointly learn spatiotemporal patterns and nutrient–phytoplankton process constraints. The N-PCLN outperforms ConvLSTM, Transformer, MDN, CNN, and LSTM models, achieving an R 2 of 0.767, an MAE of 1.483 mg/m 3 , and an RMSE of 2.665 mg/m 3 . Sparse-data experiments show that N-PCLN maintains more stable performance than the selected baseline models under reduced data availability. The ablation experiments indicate that LST is the dominant meteorological factor driver of short-term Chla dynamics, while wind speed and precipitation mainly affect hydrodynamic redistribution and runoff-related nutrient transport. Physical-loss gradient analysis further reveals that the N-P constraint acts differently across seasons and Chla concentration. These results demonstrate that N-PCLN improves both prediction performance and process interpretability. It provides a useful framework for satellite-based lake water quality prediction.

title: Cross-view guided remote sensing super-resolution via constrained residual refinement
summary: Existing RSISR reconstructs high-resolution imagery primarily from the degraded satellite observation, leaving missing fine-scale information underconstrained. We study whether geo-associated but geometrically misaligned ground imagery can provide useful auxiliary information for satellite super-resolution. We formulate Cross-View Guided Super-Resolution (CVG-SR) and propose Selective Residual Constrained Guidance (SRCG), which restricts ground-derived guidance to gated residual refinement around a satellite-conditioned reconstruction anchor. On VIGOR, matched ground guidance improves PSNR by 1.79 dB over the reconstruction anchor under realistic degradation and also outperforms fine-tuned satellite-only baselines. The advantage persists across higher magnification, different reconstruction anchors, and alternative guidance representations, while external-domain evaluations show that the effect remains observable under domain shift. The source code is available at https://github.com/zqluo-buaa/CVG-SR .

title: Diagnosing drought–flood vulnerability of rice systems across growth stages using Sentinel-1/2 and CHIRPS time series
summary: Compound and rapidly alternating drought and flood events pose a major challenge to rice production because crop impacts depend strongly on when hydroclimatic stress occurs and how crop condition evolves afterwards. Here, rice vulnerability is characterized by stage-specific exposure, sensitivity, and recovery. We developed a Stage-resolved Drought–flood Rice Vulnerability (SDRV) framework to diagnose vulnerability formation in stable single-season rice across the middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze River (MLYR), China, during 2020–2025. SDRV integrates CHIRPS precipitation and Sentinel-1/2 time-series within four regionally harmonized growth-stage windows: establishment to early tillering (S1), tillering to jointing (S2), booting/heading to grain filling (S3), and grain filling to maturity (S4). Stage-specific percentile mapping places the underlying hydroclimatic and canopy observations in a common 0–1 diagnostic space, after which the three components are integrated into stage-wise and annual vulnerability. Results show that annual vulnerability ranked as 2022 > 2025 > 2023 > 2020 > 2021 > 2024. Within the study period, drought-dominant and drought-involved pathways were associated with greater annual vulnerability than the flood-dominant pathway represented by 2020. Vulnerability amplification was concentrated mainly in S2–S3. In 2022, persistent drought-dominant stress intensified vulnerability toward S3, producing the highest annual mean vulnerability (0.599) and the largest high-vulnerability fraction (50.4%). In 2025, alternating drought and flood conditions generated a different pathway, with vulnerability concentrated in S2 and partially reduced in S3. Spatially, high vulnerability repeatedly formed a northern and central MLYR corridor, especially across Anhui, Jiangsu and adjoining parts of the middle Yangtze region. Province-level comparison with a yield-loss proxy further showed a positive external-consistency relationship for annual vulnerability after accounting for year effects. These results demonstrate that rice vulnerability under drought–flood stress develops through stage-dependent interactions among hydroclimatic forcing, canopy response, and subsequent recovery. SDRV therefore provides a process-oriented approach for identifying when and where vulnerability intensifies within the growing season.

title: Estimating Downward Shortwave Radiation over Complex Terrain: Synergizing Sentinel-2 Imagery and Topographic Data via Physics-Guided XGBoost
summary: Downward shortwave radiation (DSR) varies strongly across mountain slopes, and products designed for horizontal surfaces may not resolve this variability. We estimated slope-parallel DSR at eight Saihanba sites using Sentinel-2 imagery, topography, atmospheric inputs, and BRDF-informed surface albedo. Both branches used XGBoost, with the clear-sky branch further incorporating a parameterized radiation anchor, bounded residual learning, and support-aware output correction. On the 2024 test set (n = 1451), the full framework achieved an RMSE of 92.60 W/m2, an NRMSE of 15.79% and an R2 of 0.897. Pooled leave-one-site-out validation across all 6096 samples yielded an RMSE of 113.68 W/m2. For horizontal-surface observations at 10 Heihe River Basin stations, NRMSE was 17.60%. Clear-sky estimates depended most on solar-incidence geometry, whereas top-of-atmosphere spectra dominated the cloudy-sky XGBoost model.

title: Cross-Field Transfer of UAV-Based Winter Wheat Yield Prediction: Model Transferability and Sample Efficiency
summary: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) remote sensing is widely used for plot-scale crop yield prediction, but model performance may decline when models are transferred across fields with different crop, environmental, management, and sensing conditions. This study evaluated the cross-field transferability of UAV-based winter wheat yield models using multispectral (MS), RGB, and thermal infrared (TIR) information. Categorical Boosting (CatBoost) and multilayer perceptron (MLP) models were evaluated under five strategies: target-only training (T1), direct transfer (T2), nitrogen-based adaptation (T3), cultivar-based adaptation (T4), and mixed adaptation (T5). Direct transfer increased the normalized root mean square error (NRMSE) from 12.7% to 14.0% for CatBoost and from 12.9% to 15.9% for MLP. Mixed adaptation achieved the best overall performance, with coefficient of determination (R2) values of 0.84 and 0.87 and NRMSE values of 11.7% and 10.9% for CatBoost and MLP, respectively. After controlling for calibration sample size, the difference between T3 and T4 became smaller, indicating that adaptation performance was influenced by both calibration-data composition and sample availability. CatBoost showed diminishing returns near the 40% calibration level in this experiment, whereas MLP continued to benefit from additional target-domain samples. Prediction errors were higher for samples beyond the source-domain yield range, while mixed adaptation reduced prediction errors in both yield-range groups. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and sensor-level ablation showed that MS features provided important predictive information, while RGB and TIR provided complementary information. These results indicate that target-domain adaptation can improve cross-field UAV yield prediction and highlight the importance of calibration design, yield-range mismatch, and multi-sensor information when transferring models to new fields.

title: Effect of Sun Glints from Ice Clouds on MODIS Data Products
summary: This paper examines the way sun glints from horizontally oriented ice crystals that occur in clouds impact atmospheric data products provided by the Moderate-Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS). For this, the paper presents a statistical analysis of two years of MODIS data from all tropical land regions. The results indicate only weak glint effects on cloud amount and height, as these values are obtained using mainly observations of (inherently glint-free) thermal infrared radiation. In contrast, glints are found to cause a roughly 10% increase in mean retrieved cloud optical thickness, and 10% decreases in mean particle size and in the prevalence of ice cloud phase. Moreover, glints from undetected ice clouds are found to cause roughly 5% increases in mean aerosol optical depth and coarse mode fraction, and positive and negative biases comparable to the magnitude of the seasonal cycle in total column ozone and precipitable water vapor amounts, respectively. Given the modest size of glints, the effects are most important to consider in studies that use data from a limited range of viewing zenith angles (e.g., around nadir). The results are relevant to MODIS and to other satellite imagers that use similar retrieval algorithms, and thus likely experience similar glint effects.

title: High-Resolution Burned Area Mapping Using Sentinel-2 Imagery and Robust Satellite Techniques
summary: High accuracy in burned area (BA) mapping is desirable for many fire-related applications. Most operational products are based on coarse-resolution satellite data with a final spatial resolution ranging from 250 m to 1000 m. The use of higher-resolution satellite data, such as that from the Multispectral Imager (MSI) on board Sentinel-2, is usually reserved for generating BA products only for specific countries and time periods. Moreover, BA algorithms are typically driven by fire detection products to minimize false identifications. The resulting accuracy of such BA products depends strongly on land cover, fire regime, and the reliability of the considered fire detection products. In this paper, we exploit the multitemporal Robust Satellite Technique (RST) to identify burned areas and implement a workflow based on Sentinel-2 images within Google Earth Engine. Test results from two complete region-wide experiments conducted under contrasting seasonal, phenological, and agricultural conditions showed that 97.85% of the mapped area was confirmed as burned within the adopted multi-source validation framework, with an area-based commission error of 1.38% and omission error of 0.60%. Missed detections documented by the Regional Spatial Data Infrastructure (RSDI) amounted to 10.60 ha, corresponding to approximately 0.9% of the burned area reported by RSDI over the tested periods. Polygon-level intercomparison with RSDI and the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS) yielded Intersection over Union (IoU) values of 0.69 and 0.83, respectively. The proposed approach mapped larger burned areas than those reported by both RSDI (+48%) and EFFIS (+143%) as well.

title: A Deep Learning Framework for Nonparametric SAR Autofocus Using a Hybrid Architecture
summary: Autofocus plays a pivotal role in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging, which is particularly crucial for high-resolution applications. Traditional autofocus methods face inherent limitations, such as reliance on strong isolated scatterers within the scene or prohibitive computational complexity, making them inadequate for the practical demands of the rapid and batch processing of massive SAR imagery. Although recent deep learning (DL)-based methods have improved focusing efficiency, they predominantly rely on predefined high-order polynomial models for phase error estimation, which inevitably introduces parameter redundancy, restricts the model’s adaptability to complex phase errors, and is highly prone to inducing severe oscillations at the aperture boundaries. To overcome these limitations, this article proposes DeepAutofocus, a non-parametric deep learning framework for SAR autofocus. First, we design a physics-inspired subaperture correlation Transformer architecture. A multiscale convolutional neural network (CNN) is utilized to extract local spatial features, which are then transformed into serialized subaperture image patches. Subsequently, the self-attention mechanism of the Transformer is employed to capture the long-range dependencies across subapertures. Second, we introduce a data-driven cubic B-spline reconstruction strategy that directly estimates phase errors without depending on predefined high-order polynomial models, thereby eliminating boundary oscillations while maintaining high flexibility. Extensive experiments on both simulated and real measured satellite datasets demonstrate that, compared to traditional autofocus algorithms and existing DL-based methods, the proposed DeepAutofocus achieves superior focusing performance under various complex phase error conditions.

title: LuTan-1 InSAR-Constrained Reconstruction of Concealed Coal-Mining Working-Face Geometry
summary: To address the difficulty in determining underground working face geometry when mining records are incomplete or mining activities are concealed, this study proposes an InSAR-constrained method for inverting the geometric parameters of concealed working faces. The method uses the line-of-sight (LOS) deformation field derived from LuTan-1 InSAR observations as the primary input. The search ranges of mining depth, mining thickness, coal seam dip angle, strike azimuth, working face center coordinates, strike length, and dip length are constrained using the morphology of the subsidence basin, available empirical parameters, and the Probability Integral Method (PIM). These constraints reduce the uncertainty caused by a large search space and parameter coupling in high-dimensional inversion. An adaptive multi-strategy differential evolution algorithm is then introduced. Latin hypercube sampling is used for population initialization. Dynamic parameter adjustment, multiple mutation strategies, reflective boundary handling, and local refinement are incorporated to improve optimization stability in complex parameter spaces. The simulation results show that the proposed method generally outperforms particle swarm optimization, genetic algorithm, evolutionary strategy, and standard differential evolution in inversion accuracy, convergence stability, and robustness to errors. It can reliably recover the main geometric parameters of a predefined working face. In the engineering case study of the 97,315 working face, the inverted active-mining geometry during the LuTan-1 observation period is generally consistent with the corresponding mine records, with a deformation-fitting RMSE of 32.53 mm and relative errors of the main geometric parameters below 7.9%. Parameter sensitivity analysis further shows that the geometric dimensions and center location of the working face have pronounced effects on the LOS deformation field. These parameters should therefore be tightly constrained during inversion. The results demonstrate that the proposed method provides a feasible remote-sensing approach for identifying concealed working faces and estimating goaf geometric parameters in mining areas with incomplete records.

title: LiDAR-Assisted Survey Locates Unregistered Rock Shelters in the Blue Mountains, Australia
summary: Rock shelters are important cultural and archaeological sites in Australia, often containing evidence of Aboriginal occupation and symbolic expression. While rock shelters have been investigated across Australia, locating them in rugged environments through pedestrian surveys remains challenging. This research contributes a methodology which integrates remote sensing, GIS analyses, and archaeological survey to locate rock shelters in the Blue Mountains. We produced models in ArcGIS Pro that analyse high-resolution, UAV-based LiDAR datasets and publicly available, low-resolution, aircraft-based LiDAR datasets from the New South Wales government. Our models yield locations of potential rock shelters, which can be visually evaluated in 3D LiDAR point clouds and ground-truthed through archaeological survey. Ground-truthing confirmed the successful detection of six known rock shelters on UAV and NSW LiDAR datasets, producing more accurate coordinates than the ones listed in online databases. Significantly, we identified three previously unregistered rock shelters that preserve rock art and lithics. These promising results indicate capacity to improve the spatial accuracy of legacy site records and locate unregistered archaeological rock shelters within, and potentially beyond, Australia. Our methodology promotes targeted and efficient survey of rock shelters that can produce regional datasets benefitting local communities, archaeology, and cultural heritage management.

title: Automatic Extraction of Discontinuity Traces from Rock Mass Point Cloud Data Using PhaseVote
summary: Accurate and thorough detection of rock mass discontinuities is essential in geotechnical engineering as they have a significant impact on the stability of underground and surface excavations, yet they are difficult to automate. In the work reported here, an automatic algorithm, termed PhaseVote, is proposed for the extraction of discontinuity traces from the colour (RGB) attributes of 3D meshes which, combined with the region growing method, can help derive more accurate discontinuity modelling of a rock mass. Conventional edge detection methods degrade under low contrast and variable illumination, and geometry-based point-cloud methods overlook spectral features. The proposed approach uses contrast-invariant phase-based feature detection. The detected edges are filtered and then extended or pruned to form major discontinuity traces using the tensor voting method. The first algorithm, phase analysis, detects edges independently of local contrast, while the latter, tensor voting, links and denoises the resultant edge fragments into continuous traces using perceptual grouping. The detection capability of the proposed method is assessed by applying it to two case studies and comparing the results with an existing method. PhaseVote achieved detection rates of 94.85% and 84.72% and IoUs of 70.27% and 69.80%, compared with 76.12%/45.95% and 69.81%/43.81% for a conventional existing method. The results demonstrate that the proposed method is resilient to image contrast, robust to changes in the orientation of discontinuity planes, is less subjective and has a higher degree of automation.

title: APFNet: An Adaptive Perception Fusion Network for Multi-Scale Object Detection in Remote Sensing
summary: Accurate multi-scale object detection remains challenging in remote sensing (RS) imagery due to severe scale variation, limited pixel occupancy of small targets, and complex backgrounds. Existing multi-scale fusion methods propagate features along predefined cross-scale paths and apply receptive fields fixed once trained, so fusion weights and the spatial range of contextual evidence remain largely input-independent. The Adaptive Perception Fusion Network (APFNet) targets these two aspects through four operations: (1) Split-ELAN (SP-ELAN), a channel-compressed serial refinement backbone whose design is motivated by small-object feature preservation; (2) Adaptive Sampling (AS), which produces sample-dependent channel weights from a global descriptor during cross-scale alignment; (3) Adaptive Gating (AG), which is coupled with AS and aggregates the recalibrated features at complementary receptive-field scales; and (4) Adaptive Context Aggregation (ACA), which aligns three feature levels and applies parallel large-kernel depthwise branches to supply broader multi-scale context. On DIOR, APFNet-L achieves three-run mean values of 86.39% AP50, 63.09% AP, and 26.10% APS. A complete 23 component-group study under one scratch/no-augmentation protocol yields positive conditional contrasts for SP-ELAN, ACA, and the coupled AS–AG pathway. LEVIR and RSOD provide additional cross-dataset and configuration-selection results. These operations use established primitives; the contribution lies in their routing and aggregation.

title: Seasonal Prior-Guided Dynamic Forecasting of Nonstationary Gridded PM2.5 Concentrations in China
summary: Accurate and timely short-term forecasting of gridded PM2.5 concentrations is essential for air-quality management and public health protection, especially for the growing elderly population who are particularly vulnerable to air pollution. Advances in multi-source environmental data and deep learning have substantially improved the spatiotemporal prediction of PM2.5 concentrations. However, existing studies have mainly focused on developing increasingly sophisticated model architectures and optimization strategies while insufficiently considering the temporal nonstationarity of PM2.5 pollution and the recurrent characteristics associated with similar seasonal environmental regimes. Changes in natural environmental conditions and anthropogenic emissions can continuously alter the relationships governing PM2.5 concentrations, challenging the stability of continuous short-term forecasting; meanwhile, historically recurring seasonal pollution characteristics provide potentially valuable prior information for model adaptation. To address this problem, we propose a Seasonal Prior-guided Elastic Weight Consolidation (Seasonal EWC) framework for dynamic forecasting of nonstationary gridded PM2.5 concentrations in China. The framework derives season-specific parameter anchors and Fisher-based parameter importance from historical seasonal conditions and uses this prior knowledge to guide parameter updates during continuous short-term forecasting. Experiments with four representative spatiotemporal forecasting models showed that Seasonal EWC produced architecture-dependent changes in forecasting performance, reducing the annual mean MAE and RMSE by 30.3% and 31.7% for U-Net and by 10.9% and 7.6% for Earthformer, with only small improvements for IAM4VP and mixed changes for ConvLSTM. Parameter analysis revealed that Seasonal EWC reduced parameter-update magnitudes by approximately 27–32% and substantially limited long-term parameter deviation, indicating more stable adaptation during continuous forecasting. These findings demonstrate that seasonal prior knowledge can effectively guide dynamic model adaptation under evolving PM2.5 conditions, providing a promising approach for continuous short-term air-quality forecasting.

title: Echo-Driven Doppler Parameter Estimation for High-Resolution Squinted Spaceborne Sliding Spotlight SAR
summary: High-resolution squinted spaceborne sliding spotlight synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging requires accurate Doppler parameters. In conventional SAR processing, Doppler parameters are generally derived from prior ancillary information or estimated from the received echoes. However, Doppler parameters derived from prior information are sensitive to ancillary-measurement errors, while existing echo-based methods remain insufficient for ambiguity-resolved Doppler-centroid estimation and Doppler frequency modulation (FM)-rate refinement in high-resolution squinted sliding spotlight SAR. To reduce the reliance on prior ancillary information for Doppler-parameter determination, this paper proposes an echo-driven Doppler-parameter estimation (ED-DPE) method. The proposed method first estimates the baseband Doppler centroid using adjacent-echo cross-correlation and then resolves the Doppler ambiguity number based on the range-migration slope, thereby obtaining the absolute Doppler centroid fd. The estimated absolute Doppler centroid is subsequently used as a physical constraint on an attitude-equivalent observation geometry, which is refined through contrast-based full-aperture image formation to obtain the Doppler FM rate fr and the imaging parameters. Point-target simulations and real spaceborne SAR experiments demonstrate that the proposed ED-DPE method supports accurate focusing of 0.25-m-resolution squinted sliding spotlight SAR.

title: A Few-Shot Method Based on Spatial-Frequency Dual-Domain Feature Enhancement and Hypersphere Mapping Constraint for SAR Ship Recognition
summary: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) can acquire maritime imagery independently of daylight and under diverse weather conditions, which makes it well suited to persistent ship monitoring and maritime awareness. Nevertheless, recognizing SAR ships from only a few labeled examples remains difficult for several reasons. First, sea clutter and speckle noise may weaken ship-related structural and scattering-response information. Second, features from different categories may become difficult to separate because between-class differences are small while within-class variations remain substantial. Third, when each category contains only a few support examples, an abnormal or noisy sample can noticeably distort the estimated prototype. To address these issues, a few-shot SAR ship recognition method based on spatial-frequency dual-domain feature enhancement and hypersphere mapping constraint (SFHMC) is proposed. First, the spatial-frequency feature enhancement and extraction module (SFEE) combines the Haar discrete wavelet transform with multi-scale spatial modeling. It enhances structural, textural, and scattering-response features under complex backgrounds. Second, the hypersphere mapping constraint module (HMCM) normalizes support and query embeddings onto a unit hypersphere. By removing differences in feature magnitude, this mapping makes similarity estimation depend mainly on feature direction and produces a more structured class distribution. Third, the sample-weighted prototype generation module (SWPGM) adaptively adjusts the contribution of each support sample according to its consistency with the initial class prototype. This reduces prototype bias caused by noisy or atypical samples. The three modules jointly optimize feature representation, metric discrimination, and prototype calibration. Experiments are conducted on FUSAR-Ship and OpenSARShip, with additional validation on MSTAR under 3-way 1-shot and 3-way 5-shot settings. Compared with MBEN-BC, SFHMC improves classification accuracy by 1.41 and 1.96 percentage points on FUSAR-Ship, 2.68 and 4.46 percentage points on OpenSARShip, and 6.40 and 0.48 percentage points on MSTAR, respectively. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of SFHMC for few-shot SAR target recognition under limited data and complex imaging conditions.

title: LD-DETR: A Multi-Scale Landslide Detection and Segmentation Network for Complex Geological Environments
summary: Landslides are among the most destructive natural hazards. High-resolution remote sensing imagery provides an effective means for landslide detection and mapping, supporting geological hazard assessment and early warning. However, existing methods still face challenges in complex mountainous scenes with heterogeneous land cover and geological conditions. These challenges include irregular segmentation boundaries caused by diverse landslide shapes, small-scale detection difficulties due to background interference, and foreground–background class imbalance that hinders effective model optimization. To address these issues, we propose LD-DETR, a network for landslide detection and segmentation. An Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) module is integrated into the segmentation head to improve multi-scale feature representation, enabling better segmentation of landslides with varying spatial sizes. To alleviate class imbalance caused by the dominance of non-landslide pixels, a weighted Tversky Loss is introduced to improve the learning of hard samples. Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) is further combined with orientation-aware data augmentation to enable parameter-efficient adaptation, reducing the proportion of trainable parameters of LD-DETR to 41.07% while keeping the pre-trained backbone parameters frozen. Experiments on the Bijie and Luding Landslide Dataset (BLLD) demonstrate that LD-DETR is competitive with the baseline model and several YOLO-based approaches. The proposed method achieves an F1-score of 95.18% and a Recall of 95%, while the segmentation task reaches an mAP of 59.28%, slightly higher than the RF-DETR baseline. Furthermore, a limited-sample adaptation experiment on the Jiuzhai landslide dataset demonstrates the transferability of the proposed method across different geographic regions. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides competitive landslide detection and segmentation performance and offers an approach for fine-grained landslide mapping using remote sensing imagery.

title: Shape-Adaptive Learning and Style-Aware Decomposition for Domain-Generalized Oriented Object Detection
summary: Oriented object detection is essential for interpreting high-resolution remote-sensing images, but detectors trained on a single source domain often suffer from severe performance degradation under unseen imaging conditions. Existing domain generalization methods mainly address horizontal detection or treat style variation as an undifferentiated perturbation, while the geometry-sensitive nature of oriented objects, especially elongated instances, is insufficiently considered. To address these limitations, a shape-adaptive learning and style-aware decomposition framework, termed SA-DGOD, is proposed for single-source domain-generalized oriented object detection. A frozen CLIP image encoder is employed only during training to provide multi-level style statistics, from which several interpretable branch-style pseudo-domains are constructed by modulating feature statistics that characterize photometric and contrast variations. These explicit pseudo-domain identities enable structured style diversification without accessing target-domain data. To improve orientation-sensitive representation learning, a shape-adaptive soft consistency loss is introduced for rotated RoI features. Instead of using a fixed-threshold binary weighting scheme, the proposed loss adopts an aspect-ratio-aware threshold and a continuous rotated-IoU-based weight, allowing elongated objects and geometrically reliable proposals to be handled more flexibly. Furthermore, a style-aware common-specific classifier decomposition is introduced into the proposed framework to separate domain-invariant category discrimination from pseudo-domain-specific style bias. Extensive experiments on multiple remote sensing benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness and generalization capability of SA-DGOD.

title: Multi-Index Remote Sensing Assessment of Agro-Climatic Change and Agricultural Responses in Temperate and Semi-Arid Regions
summary: Diverse climatic regions exhibit unique agro-climatic vulnerabilities that are significantly shaped by climate stress. Understanding these distinct vulnerabilities is essential for developing effective policies to mitigate climate change impacts and ensuring sustainable environmental management. This study examines agro-climatic vulnerabilities in Nottinghamshire County (United Kingdom) and Udaipur District (India) from 2000 to 2024, comparing climate change impacts across temperate and semi-arid agricultural systems that represent fundamentally different system behaviours under contrasting climatic conditions. Using multi-temporal Landsat imagery and WorldClim climate data, nine environmental indices were analysed: the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), Vegetation Condition Index (VCI), Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI), Moisture Stress Index (MSI), Land Surface Temperature (LST), Temperature Condition Index (TCI), Vegetation Health Index (VHI), Drought Risk Index (DRI), and Crop Health Index (CHI). The results reveal contrasting regional trajectories that challenge conventional assumptions about climate vulnerability. Udaipur exhibited improved vegetation and moisture conditions across the observation period, whereas Nottinghamshire showed intensifying moisture stress and declining precipitation. Warming was more pronounced in Nottinghamshire, while strong inter-index correlations validated the monitoring approach. These findings indicate that Udaipur benefits from intensified monsoon patterns, requiring flood mitigation and water-storage infrastructure, whereas Nottinghamshire’s rising moisture stress underscores the need for sustained monitoring and adaptive management. This comparative framework provides evidence-based insights for region-specific adaptation strategies essential to sustainable agricultural development across diverse agro-climatic zones.

title: Continuous Radar QPE Bias Field Reconstruction Through the Implicit Neural Representation Framework: QPE-BiasINR
summary: Biases in high-spatiotemporal-resolution radar quantitative precipitation estimation (QPE) can substantially compromise the reliability of meteorological and hydrological disaster warning. Existing QPE correction methods commonly assume predefined spatial smoothness, whereas localized biases can vary sharply over short spatial distances. We therefore propose an implicit neural representation (INR) framework for continuous radar QPE bias-field reconstruction (QPE-BiasINR). QPE-BiasINR introduces QPE-background modulation, which conditions bias estimation on the local precipitation context to account for precipitation-dependent spatial variations in radar QPE errors. Moreover, a multiscale spatial consistency (MSC) constraint is incorporated into the loss function to explicitly strengthen spatial consistency. QPE-BiasINR was evaluated using hourly multi-radar mosaic QPE and gauge observations within the coverage of four radars in the Daqing River Basin,China, during June–September 2023. Test set performance was benchmarked against the uncorrected radar QPE, mean-field bias correction, and Kriging. QPE-BiasINR achieved the highest correlation coefficient (0.84) and the lowest root mean square error (3.29 mm) and mean absolute error (1.68 mm). Ablation experiments on QPE-BiasINR demonstrated that QPE-background modulation improved accuracy, while the MSC constraint reduced localized overcorrection. These results indicate that QPE-BiasINR can improve high-resolution radar QPE, with potential value for hydrological modeling and operational flood-risk monitoring.

title: Multisensor Analysis of Mediterranean Convective Case Studies Using EarthCARE and Meteosat Rapid Scan Observations
summary: Convection plays a key role in the Earth’s energy balance and is responsible for severe weather phenomena such as hailstorms, which cause significant damage to infrastructure and agriculture. This study investigates convective events over the Mediterranean Basin between September 2024 and September 2025 using a synergistic combination of active and passive satellite observations from geostationary (GEO) and low Earth orbit (LEO) platforms. Convective evolution is analyzed using EUMETSAT Satellite Application Facility on Support to Nowcasting and Very Short Range Forecasting products derived from Meteosat Rapid Scan Service imagery and the Multi-sensor Approach for Satellite Hail Advection (MASHA), which combines passive microwave hail probability retrievals from the Global Precipitation Measurement constellation with high-temporal-resolution Meteosat infrared observations to monitor hail-producing storms in near real time. The analysis is further enhanced with EarthCARE Cloud Profiling Radar reflectivity and Doppler velocity measurements, whose spatial variability provides a proxy for identifying convective cores and storm intensity. For selected events, observations from the Meteosat Third Generation Lightning Imager are also examined, highlighting the close relationship between intense lightning activity and strong convective updrafts. The results demonstrate the potential of combining complementary satellite observations to improve the detection and characterization of severe convection and hail-producing storms and identify the key roadblocks and pathways towards the effective integration of LEO and GEO observations.

title: Geodetic Deformation Inversion of Groundwater Variations in the Golmud River Basin, Northwestern China
summary: The Golmud River Basin is a typical inland arid river basin in the Qaidam Basin, and the dynamics of its groundwater storage are of great importance for regional ecological security and water resources management. To address the limited spatial representativeness of traditional hydrological station networks and the relatively low spatial resolution of satellite gravimetry such as the Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE), this study develops a multi-source geodetic inversion framework for groundwater estimation by using Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR), Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), and GRACE satellite gravimetry. Surface deformation with high spatial resolution over the Golmud River Basin is derived from Sentinel-1 SAR images from 2017 to 2021. After correcting for modeled non-hydrological loading effects and screening observations to reduce the influence of potential non-hydrological signals, groundwater spatiotemporal variations are inverted based on elastic loading theory. The results show that from 2017 to 2021, surface deformation in the Golmud River Basin is jointly controlled by river dynamics, mineral extraction, and urbanization, forming a spatial pattern of river corridor zones and mining-related patches. Groundwater storage shows an overall increasing trend during the study period, with a particularly significant increase in the southwestern region, reaching more than 20 mm/a. A synthetic experiment demonstrates that the proposed method can recover prescribed groundwater signals at a spatial resolution of approximately 40 km under the tested conditions. Compared with the InSAR-derived estimates, GRACE-derived groundwater variations exhibit a smaller seasonal amplitude, potentially reflecting the effects of limited spatial resolution and spatial signal smoothing. The WaterGAP Global Hydrology Model (WGHM) estimates are substantially smaller in magnitude than those derived from InSAR and GRACE, highlighting the uncertainties associated with model-based groundwater estimates in this high-altitude basin. Groundwater in the Golmud River Basin experienced a rapid increase during 2017 to 2019, which is likely driven by increased precipitation and lower temperatures associated with a La Niña event, indicating a teleconnection between global climate variability and regional water resource changes. This study provides a technical reference for refined groundwater monitoring at a tens-of-kilometers scale in small and medium-scale arid basin systems.

title: Enhanced Quantitative Precipitation Estimation During Typhoon Storms Based on Optimized Dual-Polarimetric Radar Quality Control
summary: Accurate radar-based quantitative precipitation estimation (QPE) plays a critical role in disaster prevention and reduction. In mountainous terrain, blockage of low-elevation radar beams can lead to missing low-level precipitation observations, while errors in specific differential phase KDP retrieval further limit QPE accuracy. To address these issues, this study uses data from two S-band dual-polarization weather radars located in Fangchenggang and Beihai, together with ground rain gauges, local raindrop size distribution (DSD) data, and digital elevation model (DEM) data. Hybrid-scan elevation construction and dual-radar mosaicking are adopted to improve the effective coverage of low-elevation observations, and a threshold-fusion strategy for KDP, denoted as KDP_TF, is proposed. The strategy selects the larger of the conventionally quality-controlled KDP_QC and variationally reconstructed KDP_VR at each valid gate. Based on the CSU-HIDRO algorithm, three QPE products, namely the quality-control QPE (QC_QPE), the variational-reconstruction QPE (VR_QPE), and the threshold-fusion QPE (TF_QPE), are generated. The precipitation events associated with Typhoon Yagi in 2024 and Typhoon Matmo in 2025 are selected for evaluation. The results indicate that TF_QPE most effectively mitigates the underestimation of 24 h accumulated precipitation. Compared with QC_QPE, the magnitude of the negative relative bias (RB) of TF_QPE is reduced, from −27.30% to −20.07% and from −16.56% to −9.78%, respectively, for the Yagi and Matmo events; the root-mean-square error (RMSE) decreases from 46.76 to 43.79 mm and from 43.27 to 43.13 mm, respectively. The hourly precipitation results further show that TF_QPE better captures the peak intensity of heavy precipitation and exhibits no evident temporal lag relative to rain gauge observations. For the heavy precipitation category, TF_QPE also yields the highest probability of detection (POD) and critical success index (CSI). These results suggest that the QPE framework developed in this study, which integrates hybrid-scan elevation construction, dual-radar mosaicking, and threshold-fusion-based KDP optimization, can improve the effective low-elevation observational coverage in mountainous terrain and mitigate the underestimation of typhoon-induced heavy precipitation in radar QPE. These results provide technical references for typhoon-related heavy-rainfall monitoring and flood early-warning as well as radar-QPE applications over coastal Guangxi.

title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Multi-Location ABL Wind Profiling with Minimal Instrumentation
summary: The vertical wind profile within the Atmospheric Boundary Layer (ABL) is a critical variable for a wide range of applications, including wind energy, air traffic and Unmanned Aerial System (UAS) management, pollutant dispersion, and urban air mobility. However, its accurate characterization typically requires expensive vertical-profiling LiDAR instruments, which limits the number of locations that can be simultaneously monitored. Building upon previous work in which machine-learning algorithms were trained on LiDAR data from the University of León (Spain) to reconstruct full ABL wind profiles from a single near-surface measurement, this study replaces the traditional data-driven neural network approach with Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), embedding a physical constraint directly into the loss function as evaluated by automatic differentiation, and tests two such constraints under architectural control: the Ekman boundary-layer momentum balance, closed with a Monin–Obukhov eddy viscosity, and a shear-constrained formulation based on a power-law profile with an inferred exponent. With dense supervision at the target heights, neither constraint improves on an architecture-matched network without a physical term (RMSE 1.35–1.36 m/s, direction MAE 20.1–20.4∘ across all three, Kruskal–Wallis p=0.0125). In a vertical-extrapolation protocol, training with gates up to 111 m, selecting models by their skill at 140 m, and testing blind on 170–300 m, the Ekman constraint shows no detectable advantage over its own architectural control. In contrast, the shear-constrained model does, reaching 1.80±0.01 m/s speed RMSE and 27.0∘±0.3∘ direction MAE against 2.66±0.10 m/s and 34.2∘±1.8∘ for the Ekman-constrained arm and 2.61±0.12 m/s and 33.9∘±2.0∘ for the physics-free arm, which are statistically indistinguishable from one another; the shear-constrained gain is confirmed against its own architectural control (2.64±0.08 m/s, 33.0∘±1.8∘, matching the physics-free arm), ruling out the additional output as the explanation, and converts an erratic extrapolator into a stable one. The results are consistent with the benefit of embedding physics into the loss being therefore specific to the extrapolation regime and to the formulation tested, not a generic property of physics-informed learning. These findings are based on data from a single suburban site, and multi-site validation remains necessary before they can be generalized. By eliminating the need for continuous LiDAR operation after the training phase, the proposed methodology aims to enable cost-effective monitoring of multiple locations with a single instrument.

title: Assessing Spatio-Temporal Patterns and Statistical Associations of Meteorological and Agricultural Droughts in Winter Wheat Using Multi-Source Data
summary: Characterizing the spatiotemporal differences between meteorological and agricultural drought is important for drought monitoring and risk management in major grain-producing regions. However, coordinated assessment of meteorological anomalies and crop moisture responses using multi-source data remains challenging. In this study, an integrated multi-source framework was developed to jointly characterize meteorological and agricultural drought in winter wheat across six selected growing seasons in Henan Province, China. The standardized precipitation index (SPI) and vegetation water index (VWI) were used to characterize meteorological and agricultural drought, respectively. Furthermore, standard deviational ellipse analysis and center-based spatial statistics were used to characterize drought distribution, orientation, and spatial migration, while Pearson correlation analysis was used to examine statistical associations among SPI-defined drought, VWI-defined drought, and effective irrigated area. Across the selected study periods, meteorological and agricultural drought showed distinct temporal and spatial patterns. In addition, the SPI–VWI association varied with drought severity: light drought showed the strongest positive association (r = 0.64), moderate drought showed a weak negative association (r = −0.20), and severe drought showed a moderate positive association (r = 0.57). The association between total SPI- and VWI-defined drought areas was weak (r = −0.07). At the common 1-km analysis scale, VWI-defined agricultural drought maintained a more stable spatial center and major-axis orientation than SPI-defined meteorological drought, while the difference in ellipse extent was more pronounced in the earlier study periods and narrowed markedly in the later periods. Effective irrigated area showed an exploratory negative association with total VWI-defined agricultural drought area (r = −0.72, p = 0.11; n = 6); although the association did not reach conventional statistical significance, its direction identifies irrigation conditions as relevant contextual information when interpreting variations in agricultural drought. The integrated framework provides a complementary basis for jointly assessing meteorological stress and crop moisture conditions and may support drought-risk assessment and irrigation management in major winter wheat-producing regions.

title: MCI-DETR: A Multi-Level Context Interaction Transformer for Small-Object Detection in UAV Imagery
summary: Small objects in UAV imagery often exhibit weak visual representations, suffer from background clutter, and receive insufficient cross-scale feature interaction. To address these challenges, we develop MCI-DETR, a multi-level contextual interaction detector built upon RT-DETR. First, a Local-Context Modulated Interaction Module (LCMI) is designed to selectively modulate contextual features using local structural responses, thereby suppressing irrelevant background responses while expanding the effective receptive field. Second, CATM is incorporated into the high-level feature interaction stage to form a Context Interaction Module (CCIM), strengthening target-related information through spatial- and channel-domain context mapping and additive Query–Key interaction and reducing the interference of complex backgrounds with the high-level semantic representation of weak small objects. Finally, a Multi-Scale Adaptive Gated Fusion Module (MSAGF) is designed to dynamically adjust the fusion contributions of information at different scales according to the input features, while improving the quality of cross-scale feature fusion through gated coordination between local details and global context. On VisDrone2019, MCI-DETR surpasses RT-DETR by 5.2%, 4.8%, and 3.2% in mAP50, mAP50-95, and APS, respectively, demonstrating enhanced robustness for small-object recognition in cluttered aerial imagery. MCI-DETR also achieves competitive performance on UAVDT and HIT-UAV against representative detectors, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed design under different UAV scenes and imaging conditions. Overall, MCI-DETR strengthens the representation of small objects in aerial scenes and maintains reliable detection performance in the presence of cluttered backgrounds.

title: Mapping Seasonal and Persistent Surface-Current Regimes Using Long-Term HF Radar Observations and Physics-Guided Clustering
summary: Long-term high-frequency radar (HFR) observations provide a unique opportunity to examine how coastal surface currents organise into recurrent current-field configurations. This study uses the 2013–2024 HFR-Lisbon surface-current record to identify sub-inertial regimes in the Lisbon coastal region, a dynamically complex sector of the western Iberian margin. Hourly HFR currents were quality controlled, filtered with a centred 33 h rolling mean and restricted to a sub-inertial analysis domain defined from long-term coverage and residual semidiurnal-energy criteria. A physics-guided K-means clustering approach was then applied to seven physically interpretable descriptors of current intensity, directional coherence, spatial contrast, temporal change and bathymetry-based current-speed distribution. Four recurrent regimes were identified: a low-energy regime, a shelf-intensified regime, a moderate slope/offshore regime and an energetic offshore-intensified regime. The regimes show coherent spatial structures, marked seasonal organisation, persistence over several days and preferential temporal pathways. ERA5 winds, analysed a posteriori, show the strongest contrast between the low-energy regime, associated primarily with weaker-than-average winds, and the energetic offshore-intensified regime, associated with stronger and more northerly wind conditions. The results demonstrate the value of long-term HFR observations and physics-guided clustering for identifying and interpreting recurrent coastal surface-current configurations.
